title: Arrange Done ad hoc sessions directly for delivery observation and publication

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: SEED-413#arrange-done-ad-hoc-observation-and-publication (plan 730-arrange-done-ad-hoc-observation-and-publication), completed revision fd378d80897fd61c9741cf2ee5d139ab788694dc. Checked in an isolated detached scratch worktree, set up with `npm ci` on Node 24.21.0 to match .node-version. The story worktree was not touched.

Promise checked (the suggested one held): commitments 12a and 12b. While inspection of one Done branch's delivery is held, deleting or expiring that branch wins. After release the other branch's delivery still settles, the removed record stays absent, and only the survivor keeps its landing pins.

Fault: dashboard/server/observedSessionLandings.ts, captureObservedLandings. A `settled` flag was set inside the changeSessionRecord callback. After the store write, `if (!settled) landing = await keepManualLanding(record, pair);` was added. So when the record had been deleted or expired during the held inspection, the observation still recorded the landing pins from its stale snapshot. In other words, the fault skipped the check that the record still exists when settling. The store write path (launchRecordStore.changeSessionRecord) was left unchanged. Fixtures and assertions were left unchanged.

Maintained checks: dashboard/backend-tests/review/ad-hoc-manual-landing-observation-lifecycle.spec.ts, both cases. The command was `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES caffeinate -i npm run test:dashboard:backend -- review/ad-hoc-manual-landing-observation-lifecycle.spec.ts --workers=1`, with OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_BACKEND_PROOF_RECORD set.
- Baseline: proof record showed selectedCount 2 and both passed (3511 ms, 3315 ms). Runner and strict status both passed. Load average 14.1 to 15.5.
- Faulted: both tests failed (4848 ms, 4027 ms). Each failed at expectOnlyTheSurvivorDelivered, at `expect(landingPins(checkout.integration)).toEqual([`${pinned}/base`, `${pinned}/revision`])` (spec line 77). It received 4 refs/open-dough/one-shot/... pins where the survivor's 2 were expected; the extra base/revision pair belonged to the removed launch. Earlier assertions in the same helper passed: kept records were only the survivor, and the removed session had no branch pins. So the catch comes from the landing-pin assertion alone. Load average 17.7.
- Restored: both tests passed (3337 ms, 3339 ms). Proof record showed selectedCount 2 and runner and strict status passed. Load average 17.5 to 18.0. No timeouts in any run.

Independent witness: a scratch-only spec with no assertions on the outcome copied the maintained held-observation setup. It deleted or expired `leaving` while inspection was held, released it, awaited the observation, and then wrote kept sessions, landing pins and the leaving branch pins to JSON before any review call.
- Under the fault, both delete and expiry showed kept = [isolated-staying] and leavingBranchPins = [], but 4 landing pins: one landing pair for the removed launch on top of the survivor's.
- With the fault removed, the same witness showed kept = [isolated-staying] and 2 landing pins in both cases.
So the fault produced the promised wrong behavior on the intended path: the removed record's delivery pins reappeared and were kept. The record itself was not recreated.

Restoration: `git checkout --` restored the production file, and the scratch witness and the test-results output were deleted. `git diff` was empty, `git status --short` was empty, and HEAD stayed at fd378d808. The restored focused run passed (above). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force` followed by `git worktree prune`.

Limits: this checks only the landing-pin leak after the record is removed. It does not cover a fault that recreates the record itself. The maintained keptRecords assertion would be the observer for that, but this probe did not exercise it.

Next proof action: none required for this promise. Keep the landing-pin assertion as the observer of 12a and 12b. No already-planned repair matches this finding.

Cost:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest wall Duration per run): baseline 10.38 s, faulted 11.18 s, restored 7.48 s. Two scratch witness runs were about 8 s and 6 s (per-test durations, estimated from those). Total about 43 s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported token or time measure is available to this agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 153481 ms (measured), from 1795175070000 to 1795175223481 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision fd378d80897fd61c9741cf2ee5d139ab788694dc; verdict Caught (commitments 12a/12b, landing-pin assertion in ad-hoc-manual-landing-observation-lifecycle.spec.ts); no follow-up.
